claims.assertion: This was a rider-initiated cancellation on an instant booking (RydeX), so the only route to a lawful $6.61 cancellation fee is NS-4: cancelling within 3:00 of matching is free, later is chargeable.

The rider cancelled at 09:09:10, 9 min 0 s after acceptance at 09:00:10, i.e. beyond the 3-minute free-cancellation window, so the $6.61 fee is correctly levied under NS-4 and no refund is due on that basis.

The rider's chat message at 09:05 ('give me 2 more minutes') does not create a right to free cancellation: NS-4 makes the 3-minute window from matching the only test, and Ryde publishes no driver-late / rider-notice waiver, so a statement alone cannot defeat the fee.

The driver-side no-show requirements are in fact met on the system records: the driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 09:03:00 while 39 m from the pickup point, and remained within 200 m for 6 min 10 s (well over 3:01), so the fee would also be sustainable if the cancellation were treated as a driver-side no-show.
There is no safety or threat element in the chat or driver statement, so escalation under SAFE is not available and the dispute resolves to a fee question only.

The only non-policy ground left for the rider is Ryde's discretionary voucher remedy: the fee ($6.61) is a cancellation-fee item eligible for a RydeHELP waiver voucher, and the dispute was filed well inside the 30-day window (trip date = filing).

No account flag against the rider is warranted: her 90-day history shows 3 disputes with 0 upheld (route: 0, no-show: 0), so there is no repeated-violation pattern to trigger RD-6-type account review.

weaknesses: The decisive system records defeat the rider's core grievance: F4 shows the rider cancelled 9 min 0 s after matching (beyond the 3:00 NS-4 window) and F8 confirms $6.61 was charged, so NS-4 mandates 'no_action' rather than a refund.

The chat statement the rider relies on (F11, 09:05 'give me 2 more minutes') is contradicted in effect by the timeline: the rider then took 4 more minutes and cancelled at 09:09:10 (F4), and a statement cannot override timeline/gps records.

The driver's compliance records cut the other way: F6 (tapped 'I'm Here' 09:03:00, 39 m away) and F2/F3 (within 200 m for 6 min 30 s, stationary 6 min 10 s at 39 m) satisfy NS-1(i)-(iii), so the fee survives even under the no-show branch; the driver's long clean history (F18, 0 disputes in 1600 days) reinforces that.

The only relief realistically available is Ryde's own discretion under NS-7 (voucher, non-cash), which the policy frames as a recommendation, not an entitlement — Ryde 'reserves its absolute discretion'.

events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.88)
events.body:
The case is a rider-side cancellation on an instant RydeX booking, so it enters the NS group only through NS-0's rider branch [F4][NS-0]. On that branch NS-4 is the sole test: cancellations made within 3:00 of matching are not chargeable, and later cancellations carry the $6.61 fee [F4][NS-4]. The timeline shows acceptance at 09:00:10 and rider cancellation at 09:09:10 — 9 min 0 s (540 s), far beyond the 3:00 free window — and the fare record confirms $6.61 was charged, with no surge multiplier [F4][F8][F9][NS-4]. NS-4 therefore mandates no_action, and the rider's own advocate concedes this (C2) [F4][NS-4].

The rider's grievance is that she messaged at 09:05 saying she was two more minutes away [F11]. A statement cannot override the timeline and fare records: the chronology shows the driver had already been on scene since 09:02:40 and she cancelled 4 min after her message [F2][F4][F11][NS-4]. Ryde publishes no driver-late or rider-notice waiver of the 3-minute window, so the message creates no refund entitlement; it only bears on Ryde's discretion under NS-7 [F11][NS-4][NS-7].

The driver-side no-show branch is corroborative only and not needed to sustain the fee, but the records support it: closest approach 39 m, first within 200 m at 09:02:40, stationary 6 min 10 s at 39 m, cumulative 6 min 30 s within 200 m, and an arrival recorded at 09:02:40 [F1][F2][F3][F5][NS-1]. certificate: ✓ NS-4 rider cancelled more than 3 min after matching [case] 540 s after acceptance (F4)

what_would_change: Had the rider cancelled within 3 minutes of matching, NS-4 would have waived the $6.61 fee.

claims.assertion: This was a rider-initiated cancellation on an instant booking (RydeX), so the only route to a lawful $6.61 cancellation fee is NS-4: cancelling within 3:00 of matching is free, later is chargeable.

The rider cancelled at 09:09:10, 9 min 0 s after acceptance at 09:00:10, i.e. beyond the 3-minute free-cancellation window, so the $6.61 fee is correctly levied under NS-4 and no refund is due on that basis.

The rider's chat message at 09:05 ('give me 2 more minutes') does not create a right to free cancellation: NS-4 makes the 3-minute window from matching the only test, and Ryde publishes no driver-late / rider-notice waiver, so a statement alone cannot defeat the fee.

The driver-side no-show requirements are in fact met on the system records: the driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 09:03:00 while 39 m from the pickup point, and remained within 200 m for 6 min 10 s (well over 3:01), so the fee would also be sustainable if the cancellation were treated as a driver-side no-show.
There is no safety or threat element in the chat or driver statement, so escalation under SAFE is not available and the dispute resolves to a fee question only.

The only non-policy ground left for the rider is Ryde's discretionary voucher remedy: the fee ($6.61) is a cancellation-fee item eligible for a RydeHELP waiver voucher, and the dispute was filed well inside the 30-day window (trip date = filing).

No account flag against the rider is warranted: her 90-day history shows 3 disputes with 0 upheld (route: 0, no-show: 0), so there is no repeated-violation pattern to trigger RD-6-type account review.

weaknesses: The decisive system records defeat the rider's core grievance: F4 shows the rider cancelled 9 min 0 s after matching (beyond the 3:00 NS-4 window) and F8 confirms $6.61 was charged, so NS-4 mandates 'no_action' rather than a refund.

The chat statement the rider relies on (F11, 09:05 'give me 2 more minutes') is contradicted in effect by the timeline: the rider then took 4 more minutes and cancelled at 09:09:10 (F4), and a statement cannot override timeline/gps records.

The driver's compliance records cut the other way: F6 (tapped 'I'm Here' 09:03:00, 39 m away) and F2/F3 (within 200 m for 6 min 30 s, stationary 6 min 10 s at 39 m) satisfy NS-1(i)-(iii), so the fee survives even under the no-show branch; the driver's long clean history (F18, 0 disputes in 1600 days) reinforces that.

The only relief realistically available is Ryde's own discretion under NS-7 (voucher, non-cash), which the policy frames as a recommendation, not an entitlement — Ryde 'reserves its absolute discretion'.

claims.assertion: The driver reached the pickup point: his closest approach was 39 m and he was first within 200 m of Tanjong Pagar Centre at 09:02:40, so he was at the pickup location in GPS terms.

The driver waited on scene: he was stationary 09:03:00–09:09:10 (6 min 10 s) at a point 39 m from the pickup, and cumulative time within 200 m before the rider's cancellation was 6 min 30 s, both well over the 3-minute threshold (within_200m_s > 180).

The driver pressed "I'm Here" at 09:03:00, 39 m from the pickup point, and stayed within 200 m for the following 6 min 10 s, satisfying the arrival-button requirement; the contradicting timeline entry F7 (press = null) conflicts with the GPS-backed arrival record and is outweighed by it.

The cancellation was the rider's: she cancelled at 09:09:10, 9 minutes after acceptance, i.e. 6 min 30 s after the driver was recorded at the pickup — far beyond the 3-minute no-charge window for rider cancellations.

The rider's own message at 09:05 asked for "2 more minutes", yet she cancelled four minutes later at 09:09:10, so the delay was hers; chat also shows the driver announcing his arrival at 09:03 and calling twice.
The $6.61 cancellation fee is supported by the fare record (no surge, multiplier 1.0x) and equals the published rider cancellation fee, so no amount is refundable and the driver's $4.50 share stands.

No aggravating or mitigating traffic factor applies: no incidents were recorded near the route and conditions were fair, so nothing outside the driver's control explains the rider's 9-minute delay in boarding.

The driver's record is clean (4.4 years on platform, rating 4.9, 700 trips in 90 days, 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days), supporting no account action against him and showing no pattern of cancellation-fee abuse.

weaknesses: Timeline fact F7 states the driver never tapped "I'm Here" (driver_pressed_here_at is null), which directly contradicts F6; the rider will argue NS-1(i) fails and therefore NS-2 requires a full refund of the $6.61.

The rider will cite her chat message F11 ("give me 2 more minutes") and argue she was on her way, and profile F17 shows she has filed 3 disputes in 90 days — she will use that to frame herself as a diligent commuter rather than a no-show, even though none of those disputes was upheld.
The 39 m closest-approach figure in F1 comes with no published Ryde radius (policy gap G2), so the rider can argue GPS placement at the pickup point is unproven on Ryde's own unstated standard.

points.response: Conceded on the GPS point: F1 (closest approach 39 m) and F2 (first within 200 m at 09:02:40) do place the driver at the pickup in GPS terms, but this only speaks to NS-1(ii) and does not decide whether any fee was chargeable at all. However, my client's own brief already accepts NS-4 governs here, so this concession helps only the driver's narrative, not the outcome.
Conceded: F2 (6 min 30 s cumulative within 200 m) and F3 (stationary 6 min 10 s at 39 m from 09:03:00 to 09:09:10) exceed 3:01, so NS-1(iii) is met; the driver waited on scene.

This claim is void as pleaded: D3 invites the judge to prefer F6 (press at 09:03:00) over F7 (driver_pressed_here_at is null) when both are the same source type, and NS-1(i) requires the press as an established fact, not a best-guess between two conflicting timeline entries. Either way the fee's validity does not depend on the press in this case, because the cancellation was made by the rider (F4), which routes the charge through NS-0 and NS-4, not NS-1.
Accepted as to the timeline: F4 shows the rider cancelled at 09:09:10, 9 min 0 s after matching, so NS-4 permits the $6.61 fee against a rider-cancelled instant booking — this is also my brief's C2.

Largely conceded: F11 (09:05, '2 more minutes') followed by cancellation at 09:09:10 (F4) shows the delay was my client's, and F10/F12 show the driver announced arrival at 09:03 and called twice. The one rider-side point preserved is that F11 is a genuine attempt to board, not a refusal, which is relevant only to Ryde's discretionary voucher under NS-7, not to a refund entitlement.

Conceded on quantum and liability: F8 ($6.61 charged) and F9 (multiplier 1.0×, no surge) match the published rider cancellation fee and no alternative figure is computable from the fare records, so the base fee is not refundable. My client's request stands as 'no_action' with only a discretionary voucher under NS-7.

Accepted: F15 shows no incidents near the route and F16 records fair weather with 0.0 mm rain, so no external factor excuses the delay; F14 (Anson Road band 4, 30–39 km/h) is ordinary flowing traffic and is not incident evidence under RD-4.

Accepted that the driver's record is clean (F18: 4.4 years, rating 4.9, 700 trips, 0 disputes, 0 upheld) and no account action is sought against him; my client likewise seeks no flag, since F17 shows 3 disputes with 0 upheld and no repeated-violation pattern.

I keep C2 on the record: NS-4 makes the 3:00 window from matching the only test for a rider-side instant cancellation and it fails on F4, so my client's refund claim cannot be supported and I maintain 'no_action' rather than pressing a refund I cannot prove.
Agreed on the routing: a rider-initiated cancellation on an instant RydeX booking is governed by NS-0 via NS-4, and the driver does not need the no-show branch to sustain the fee.

This is the core of the driver's case and the rider herself concedes it: cancellation at 09:09:10 is 9 min 0 s after acceptance at 09:00:10, far beyond the 3:00 free window of NS-4, so the $6.61 fee is correctly levied and no_action is the right outcome.

The driver relies on the rider's own concession here: her 09:05 message asking for '2 more minutes' creates no waiver of the NS-4 window, and the fare record shows the $6.61 was charged without any unpublished add-on.

The driver accepts the rider's corroboration that the no-show requirements are met on the system records — 'I'm Here' at 09:03:00 at 39 m and 6 min 30 s within 200 m — but notes the timeline field F7 (no press recorded) conflicts with F6, and the GPS-supported arrival records are the stronger evidence, so the fee stands on either branch.
The driver agrees that nothing in the chat or the driver's statement involves a threat, so no SAFE escalation applies and the case resolves purely as a fee question.

NS-7 is a discretionary rider-side waiver channel, not an entitlement, and it cannot override NS-4's mandatory result that a cancellation 9 min after matching is chargeable; the driver therefore asks the tribunal to keep the outcome at no_action rather than route the rider to a voucher.

No account flag is sought against the rider and none against the driver: both profiles show 0 disputes upheld in 90 days (rider F17, driver F18), so the additional action under RD-6 is inapplicable to either party.
